doors.note: Configured page (Shopify, og:site_name "The Boatslip", one JSON-LD Organization node). The static HTML holds no events: the calendar is an Elfsight widget (<div class="elfsight-app-588829d7-aa7e-42e8-8c6d-df5b85ccca54">, static.elfsight.com/platform/platform.js) read by collectElfsightCalendarEvents. The footer prints "161 Commercial Street Provincetown, MA 02657" and links instagram.com/boatslipresort.

doors.truthFlag: the boot payload carries the widget’s entire event list: 232 entries, past and future, no paging
doors.note: Elfsight event-calendar app. Entries: name, start/end { date, time } with timeZone America/New_York on every dated entry, repeatPeriod (noRepeat 230, custom 2), description (HTML), coverImage, eventType ids (Tea Dance 161, Beach Club 20, Buoy Bar 5, plus ids no longer in the type list), location ids into settings.locations (The Boatslip / The Beach Club / The Buoy Bar, all 161 Commercial Street). No actions (ticket buttons) on any entry. Five 2025 entries store start/end as epoch milliseconds with timeZone null instead of { date, time }; four entries carry visible:false.

recon.notes: Recon from one read of each door on 2026-10-18 (the validation run read both again, 2 live requests). 232 entries: 4 hidden (visible:false, 2 of them future), 5 legacy epoch-stamped rows (May 2025), 2 "custom" daily repeats (pool-party weeks that ended 2026-07-16 and 2026-08-21), 108 visible one-offs on or after 2026-10-18 (11 left in 2026, 97 dated for the 2027 season, 2027-05-07..2027-08-31), 16 one-offs that ended in the 30 days before recon, 97 one-offs that ended earlier (archive).

coverage.basis: Feed door: the Elfsight boot payload lists every entry the widget renders (232). Documented: every visible one-off whose last day is on or after 2026-10-18 (108 singles; the 2027 season is already dated and singles are never window-limited). Not documented, counted: 97 one-offs ended before 2026-09-18 (archive), 16 ended between 2026-09-18 and 2026-10-17 (recent past, kept by the scraper under allowPastEvents), 2 repeating pool-party entries whose rules ended in summer, 5 legacy epoch rows from 2025, 4 hidden entries. No series: the widget states no repeat on any upcoming entry (every tea dance is hand-entered per afternoon). The page's own HTML carries none of this.

traps.why: An older entry shape; all five are from the 2025 season. buildEventFromElfsightRow needs start.date and returns nothing for them, and the archive filter cannot read their day either, so they are read and then dropped — correct for 17-month-old nights, but a reader that converted the epoch would resurrect them.

traps.label: "SUBMERGED POOL PARTY" (daily 2026-08-17..21) and "CANNON BALL POOL PARTY" (daily 2026-07-11..16), repeatPeriod "custom"
traps.why: The only repeating entries in the widget; both rules end in summer 2026. The archive filter keeps repeating entries for their rule to decide, and the expander finds no night in the next 90 days — "a widget entry that has run out, not an event".

traps.label: 16 tea dances that ended between 2026-09-18 and 2026-10-17 (DOG TAG TEA 2026-09-18 .. HEATED RIVAL-TEA 2026-10-17)
traps.why: Less than 30 days old, so the Elfsight archive rule leaves them in and allowPastEvents keeps them: extraction is correct behaviour, not a bug. Documented so a diff does not count 16 extra events as ghosts.
traps.note: Validation run 2026-10-18: 131 rows read after the archive filter = 108 upcoming + 16 recent past + 5 epoch rows + 2 run-out repeats; 126 events built. One of these, "DOG TAG TEA - Mates Leather Weekend" (2026-10-02), was kept as bear and then grouped by the cadence pass into FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR with the other Friday DOG TAG TEAs and offered as a series card (seriesWrites report mode).

openQuestions.q: The widget already dates the whole 2027 season (97 singles from 2027-05-07). With daysToLookAhead null the run builds all of them and bear-checks all of them (121 of 126 dropped as general tea dances). Should a venue widget's next-season entries wait for a horizon, or is seven months out fine for a seasonal town?

The promoter registry matched "Spooky Bear" in four tea titles and replaced the venue website with ursamen.org/spookybear (🔗 LINKS: "the source site’s front door yields to the promoter the event names"). These are the Boatslip’s own afternoon teas during that weekend, not Northeast Ursamen productions — is the swap wanted on a venue site’s own programme?

The cadence pass grouped the hand-entered Friday DOG TAG TEAs into FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR and hung the rule on the one that survived the bear check, "DOG TAG TEA - Mates Leather Weekend" (a themed edition), offering it as a weekly series card. The widget states no repeat; every afternoon is its own entry.
